en.html:
I lay there, staring at the ceiling.
Nothing else to do. Sleeping also I could not manage.

The sliding door was still open. Wind came in from the garden, chilly enough, but that was not what kept me awake. If anything, it felt good.
Still, no sleep.

Then get up, simple. Except with one leg injured, even getting up was too much bother. Almost no pain now, yes—but that arrangement depended very clearly on my not moving. Why go and spoil a working arrangement?

So after considering the alternatives, lying there was the alternative.
With all this heat inside me.

ja.html:
寝転がって、天井を見つめる。
　ほかにできることがない。
　眠ることさえ。

　開け放したままのがらり戸は庭からの風を運び、肌
寒いほどだったが、それが寝るのに邪魔ということは
なかった。むしろ心地よい。
　けれど眠れない。

　なら起きればいいのだろうが、片足を負傷した状態
ではそれも億劫だった。痛みはもうほとんどないとは
いえ、それがじっとしていることを条件に危うく成立
しているのは明らかだ。その安息を捨てる理由もない。

　つまるところ、寝転がってる以外にないのだった。
　熱い身体を抱えながら。

en.html:
After that, the police came. Minato had probably arranged it. They took the three of us into protection.

Straight to the hospital, obviously.

My own treatment was only bleeding stopped, stitches, painkillers, finished. The other two, naturally, were not so lucky. I could not see them through it, but I was told they had been sent to intensive care.

They were probably still there. I had announced that I would stay until the operations were over, but every person present shouted at me to go home and sleep. Surrender was my only option.

I knew myself that I could do nothing useful and would only be in the way. Uncle and Auntie and Tadayasu's family were arriving just as I was leaving, and a police car dropped me home, alone.

And now here I was, listening to the night wind.

ja.html:
あれから。
　湊斗さんが手配していたのだろう。警察がやってき
て、おれたちは保護された。

　そのまま病院へ直行だったのは言うまでもない。

　おれの治療は止血と縫合、鎮痛剤投与だけで済んで
しまったが、他の二人は当然そうはいかなかった。
　見届けることはできなかったが、集中治療室へ送ら
れたと聞かされている。

　おそらく、今もまだそこにいるだろう。
　手術が終わるまで自分も残ると言うだけ言ってみた
が、その場にいた全員に帰って寝ろと怒られては断念
するしかなかった。

　何の役にも立てないどころか、邪魔にしかならない
ことは自分でもわかっていたから仕方がない。
　おれはおじさんおばさん、忠保の家族らと入れ違う
形で、警察の車に送られてひとり帰ってきた。

　そうして、今はここでこうして夜風を聴いている。

en.html:
There was a lot I needed to think about. Uncle and Auntie, Tadayasu's family: I would have to explain things to them in my own words, even if the police had told them already. Oh, and the police. They would want my statement also.

At the hospital nobody had asked me anything. Probably they were being considerate, but I could not keep leaning on that. Of the three of us I was the closest to unharmed, so the duty of explaining was mine.

Whatever I saw, whatever happened, I had to tell them correctly, however painful. I should prepare beforehand. Explaining is not exactly my strong subject.

And there were countless other things. Starting with what to do about breakfast tomorrow morning... all the way up to that Suzukawa.

And my friends.

ja.html:
考えるべきことは多くあった。
　おじさんおばさん、忠保の家族にも、おれの口から
事の説明をしなくてはならないだろう。警察から既に
聞いていても――そうか、警察の事情聴取もある。

　病院では誰もおれに何も訊かなかった。気を遣って
くれたのだろうが、甘えてはいられない。
　三人の中で一番無事に近かった人間として、おれに
は説明する義務があるはずだった。

　正しく、見たこと起きたことを彼らに伝えなくては
ならない。それが辛さを伴おうと。
　前もって準備をしておくべきだった。おれは説明事
が得意なわけではないのだから。

　他にも考えなくてはならないことはいくらでもある。
とりあえず明日の朝飯はどうしたものかといったこと
から……あの鈴川のことまで。
　そして、仲間のことも。

en.html:
Konatsu. Tadayasu. Ritsu.

The reality that had struck those three.

There was truly so much to think about. And yet my mind was holding none of it.

Tomorrow. The moment I woke in this bed tomorrow, I would accept, for the first time, that everything that happened today was real.

Then my heart would be crushed. Thinking of Konatsu's body, Tadayasu's eyes, Ritsu who was not here any more, I would fall face-down into the pillow.

I would roll across the floor and scream words with no meaning.

I knew it. I knew that was what would happen. But not now. Just now, my heart had been saved. A hot excitement was hiding the grief.

So for now, only for tonight, I would soak in this heat. I would use it to get through the sadness that starts tomorrow.

ja.html:
小夏、忠保、リツ。
　あの三人を襲った現実――――

　考えるべきことは本当に多い。
　だが今のおれはそのどれも、胸に思い描いてはいな
かった。

　明日になれば。
　明日、この寝床で目覚めたその瞬間。
　おれは初めて、今日起きたことのすべてを、本当に
現実として受け止めることになるだろう。

　そして心を押し潰されるだろう。
　小夏の体を、忠保の眼を、もういないリツを想って、
枕に突っ伏すだろう。

　床の上をのたうち、意味のない叫びを上げるだろう。

　それがわかる。
　そうなるということがわかる。
　だが今は違う。今だけは、おれの心は救われていた。
悲痛を隠してくれていた――熱い興奮が。

　だから今だけ、この一晩だけ、おれはこの熱に浸る。
　明日からの悲しみを乗り切るために。

There was one difference between yesterday's me and the me of now.

Now I had a path to believe in.

Justice. As a thought, as a concept only, nobody can believe in it from the heart. A concept is not enough. It is one sheet of paper.

That is why I had never believed in it either. I had given up. No such thing exists, I had decided.

But—

昨日までのおれと、今のおれとの違い。
　それは一つ。
　信じる道があるということ。

　正義。
　それは考えとして……概念としてあるだけでは、心
から信じることはできない。
　それでは足りないのだ。ただの紙切れだ。

　だからおれも、そんなものは信じていなかった。
　諦めていた。そんなものは無い、と。
　だけど。

en.html:
It had appeared. Justice had appeared in physical form, in a shape worth believing.

Justice means something only when someone embodies it. A person was needed who would fight under its banner.

I had never imagined such a person could exist. Fighters, warriors: when I thought of these, I could think only of the Rokuhara shogunate. A pack of starving wolves swinging brute strength wherever the appetite pointed. That was all. Rokuhara's ambition had swept over the whole world of arms.

Every powerful warrior belonged to that gang, busy suppressing the powerless. Not one warrior wanted to fight for people without strength. That is what I had thought.

But there is one. Now I know. There is a person who fights, not for his own desire, but to protect someone else.

Even if there is only one in the entire world, because he exists, I can believe in justice.

It was not a slogan. Not an empty decoration. Not one more word lazing about in dictionaries and moral science textbooks.

It was a signpost for how a person should live.

So I would walk this road, the one I could, at last, see clearly in front of me.

And then—

ja.html:
現れた。
　正義は形として現れた。
　信じるに足る姿をもって。

　正義は体現する者があって初めて意味を持つ。
　正義を奉じて戦う者が必要だったのだ。

　そんな人がいるなんて思いもしなかった。
　戦う者、武人といえば、思い浮かぶのは六波羅幕府
でしかない。欲望に任せて剛力を揮うばかりの餓狼団。
それが全て。武の世界は六波羅の野心が席巻している。

　力ある武人は総てがその一党で、力なき人々の弾圧
に奔走している。力の無い人々のために戦おうとする
武人などは一人もいない。
　そう思っていた。

　だけど、いる。
　今は知っている。
　自分の欲望ではなく、誰かを守るために、戦う人が
いることを知っている。

　それが、たった一人でも。
　おれはその人がいるのなら、正義というものを信じ
られる。

　それはただの題目ではなく。
　意味のない飾りではなく。
　国語辞典と道徳のテキストの中で惰眠を貪るだけの
一言でもなく。

　人が正しく在るための道標。

　だから、おれはこの道を行こうと思う。
　いま確かに見えているこの道筋を。



　そして――

en.html:
Sayo"Is something the matter, Miss?"
Kanae"..."
Sayo"Oho... come to think of it, Nitta's house is somewhere near here. Do you intend to stop by?"
Kanae"..."
Sayo"Miss?"
Kanae"Just now... I thought something red crossed the sky."
Sayo"Red... something?"
Kanae"Sayo. Did you not see anything?"
Sayo"You ask the impossible, Miss. If even your eyes could not make it out, how will this old woman manage? A falling star, perhaps?"
Kanae"A star... If my eyes can be trusted completely, then it looked like... a warrior."
Sayo"Ho. At night also? The shogunate gentlemen are as busy as ever. What a nuisance. An industrious tyrant: there is really nothing worse."

香奈枝 「……」
さよ 「お嬢さま？」

en.html:
Muramasa.
The deep-crimson warrior.

This was what I had wanted to see. Burned into the backs of my eyelids, every little detail—I could have remembered it easily. Still, I wanted the actual thing. To keep looking. As long as possible, as close as possible.

And here he was. Wish granted. My Muramasa, right here.
...Really? Had he really come for me?

Arre, don't be an idiot. Something about the case, he must want to ask. In this rotten world, the one and only defender of justice was hardly sitting idle. Without some business, why would he come all the way here?

...Fine, maybe concern also. Maybe he had come to see how I was.
Still, that did not give me permission to become a spoiled child. Have some shame. Cooperate, finish his business quickly, let him go.

All this excellent advice I had for myself.
Then that heroic red figure was right in front of me, and keeping quiet was no longer possible.

ja.html:
[text0140b]
　村正。
　深紅の武者。

　この姿を見たかった。
　瞼の裏に焼きついて、細部まで思い出すことも簡単
だったけれど。それでも本当の姿を見たかった。見て
いたかった。少しでも長く、少しでも近く。

　願いが叶って、おれの村正が今ここにいる。
　……まさか本当に、おれのために？

　いや、バカな。きっと事件のことでおれに聞きたい
ことかなんかがあるんだ。このロクでもない世の中、
たった一人の正義の味方が暇なはずもない。
　用事がなければおれの所なんかにわざわざ来るか。

　……そりゃまあ、心配して見に来てくれたってのも
あるかもしれないけどさ。
　だからって甘えていいもんじゃない。恥ずかしい。
協力して、手早く用件を終わらせてあげないと。

　だってのに。
　赤い雄姿をこんなに間近にしてしまったおれはもう、
我慢が利かなくなっていた。

en.html:
I looked at him. The crimson flooding his body was the color of fresh blood: ominous, yet dependable, because it declared his readiness to fight. Against the red, the golden sword shone as one brilliant point.

The austere helmet resembled an oni's face. The steel thrusting across his chest, a fortress wall.

Could any sight be more terrifying as an enemy? Could any sight bring greater relief as a protector?

Muramasa. The gentle warrior bearing an accursed name.

Looking down at me, he slowly shook his head.

　黄金造りの太刀は紅の中で一点、煌びやかに映える。

　これほど敵に回して恐ろしい姿が他にあろうか。

　呪わしい名を持つ、優しい武者。

　それは、おれを見下ろしながら。
　……ゆっくりと、かぶりを振った。

Out from behind the helmet those words spilled. A voice quiet as wind crossing an ice field.

For a moment I was blank. Then—oh, I see—I nodded inside my heart.

Honestly, this man. Would it kill him to ask other people for a little understanding and praise?

Minato. You must be very strict with yourself.

Whatever you achieve, you imagine something more perfect, a better result—Konatsu and Tadayasu and I all getting out without any injury, for example—and you cut marks from your own score.

That is why you say such things, no?

en.html: Ah...◆ damn, my eyes are blurring. Feels like I haven't got enough blood. Why, though? I shouldn't have lost all that much. Tiredness after all, maybe? I want to get up. Can't get up. As if my body's gone off somewhere. Not even one finger will move. Pathetic. Only my eyes still work. So at least let me look properly at Muramasa... but with this blur, even that I can't do. Why is it all so blurry?
en.text:
Ah...◆ damn, my eyes are blurring.

Feels like I haven't got enough blood.
Why, though? I shouldn't have lost all that much. Tiredness after all, maybe?

I want to get up. Can't get up.
As if my body's gone off somewhere. Not even one finger will move. Pathetic.

Only my eyes still work.
So at least let me look properly at Muramasa... but with this blur, even that I can't do.

Why is it all so blurry?

ja.html: ああ……◆くそ、眼が霞む。 　なんか血が足りてないみたいな感じだ。 　なんでだろ。出血は大したことなかったはずなんだ けどな。やっぱ疲れのせいかな。 　起き上がりたいけど起き上がれない。 　体がどっかにいっちまったみたいだ。 　指一本動きゃしない。なさけねぇ。 　動くのは眼だけだ。 　だから……せめて村正の姿をしっかりと見たいのに。 こう霞んでちゃあそれもできない。 　なんでこんなにぼやけるんだよ。

What is it? Tears?

Why am I crying? What is sad? How strange...

Sad. Something is sad. So sad, so unbearably sad that the tears will not stop.

What is it? What am I—

en.html:
Ah... yes.

It is because I can no longer see Muramasa.

The tears are bending my vision, and I cannot make out his shape any more. That must be why I am sad. Sad enough to cry like this.

It will be all right. He will wait until I wake. He is kind.

So, a little sleep. If I cannot get up, there is no help for it. Sleep a little, take away the tiredness... then wake up and look at Muramasa again.

Then I will follow that figure. I will start walking.

Chasing my ideal. On the road of fighting for justice, I also—

ああ……そうか。
　村正の姿がもう見えないからだ。

　涙のせいで、視界が歪んで、もう村正の形はわから
ない。
　きっとおれはそれが哀しいんだな。
　こんなに涙をこぼすほど。

　大丈夫だって。
　起きるまで待っててくれるよ。
　この人は優しいんだから。

　だから、少し眠ろう。起きられないんじゃ仕方ない。
　少し眠って、疲れをとって……それからまた起きて、
村正の姿を見よう。

　そうして、その姿を追って。
　歩き始めよう。

　理想を追って。
　正義のために戦う道を、おれも――――
